messages:
evan: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC. We need an emergency rollback + revocation play for prewarm tokens when an operator notices residency drift during a cutover. Two goals: immediate stop of any further priming in target region, and reliable audit trail for compliance.

mia: Yep. We had a scenario where a prewarm started and then an exec requested immediate halt. We lacked a single API to revoke the in-flight token and mark the handoff as aborted.

jon: Proposal: token lifecycle should include a revocation endpoint and an "abort-handoff" signal that does two things: 1) revoke any outstanding prewarm tokens, 2) emit handoff.aborted event with reason + operator id + evidence.

rachel: Nice. Suggest tokens have state: issued -> active -> revoked -> consumed. Introspection API should return state so dataplane can immediately reject revoked tokens.

evan: For speed, revocation should flip a small in-memory flag in auth-service then propagate async to the introspection cache. But dataplane should check both local cache and call introspect if cache miss. In case of partition, default to revocation wins (fail closed).

mia: UI action: operator clicks "Abort handoff" -> system asks for reason and optional evidence (logs/notes), then posts /hand-offs/{id}/abort which returns list of token ids revoked. Also archives the preflight report so compliance can review.

jon: Add an emergency TTL override workflow: if abort happens within escalation window (default 15m), system auto-reverts routing rules and reassigns lease back to origin region in maintenance mode. Reassign should be manual-confirm for residency=required tenants.

rachel: Security thought: revocation events must be signed and immutable. We should append them to our audit ledger (WAL) with sequence id, operator, and signature. Expose ledger read-only to compliance.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: added feature flag "handoff-revoke" to staging, rollout planned for 2026-04-15 :rocket:

evan: Dataplane header conventions for prewarm requests (example):
```
X-Prewarm-Token: prw_REV_XYZ
X-Target-Region: eu-central-1
X-Action: prewarm.metadata
```
On abort, dataplane should reject with 403 TOKEN_REVOKED if introspection reports revoked.

mia: Error codes to document: 403 TOKEN_REVOKED, 403 CONSENT_MISSING, 409 REGION_MISMATCH, 410 TOKEN_EXPIRED, 423 HYDRATION_BLOCKED. Also add 424 HANDOFF_ABORTED for race conditions.

jon: Observability: emit these structured events: handoff.requested, prewarm.token.issued, prewarm.token.revoked, handoff.committed, handoff.aborted. Include token_id, lease_id, operator_id, tenant_id, reason. Store preflight CSV as artifact linked to event id.

rachel: Chaos scenario: simulate a revoked token that remains cached on dataplane for 45s. Ensure revocation wins even if some requests slip through; must have a compensating trace that marks those priming requests as "potentially non-compliant" and triggers remediation.

evan: Remediation runbook (short):
- Abort handoff: POST /hand-offs/{id}/abort with reason
- Verify prewarm.token.revoked event emitted
- Check dataplane logs for any priming calls with revoked token -> mark artifacts and notify compliance
- If secrets were hydrated, initiate escrow+wipe workflow and notify customer security

mia: KMS/secret note: if secret hydration already happened in target region, revocation can't undo that. Runbook must include customer notification and key-rewrap steps. Emphasize prevention over rollback.

jon: Implementation notes: lease-manager issues tokens; auth-service supports revocation API and publishes events; audit-ledger appends revocation record; dataplane introspects token and caches state for 30s. Use monotonic revocation counter to avoid replay.

rachel: Also add a "revoke scrub window" metric: time between revoke API call and dataplane observing revoke. Aim <5s for 95th percentile in same region.

sre-bot: incident-bot: scheduled canary test "handoff-revoke-fast-path" 2026-04-16T01:00Z

evan: Action items: Evan write short RFC addendum for revoke API + runbook; Jon protos revocation in lease-manager; Mia document customer-notify steps; Rachel add observability events + metric. I'll draft a sample abort payload for the RFC.

mia: Sample abort payload idea:
POST /hand-offs/1234/abort
Body:
{ "operator_id": "mia", "reason": "unexpected residency flag", "evidence_url": "s3://artifacts/abc.csv" }
Response: 200 { "revoked_tokens": ["prw_REV_XYZ"], "event_id": "evt_789" }

jon: Good. Also include an idempotency key on abort calls to avoid duplicate processing.

rachel: One final ask: make the abort button prominent in the operator UI and require a short confirmation delay (3s) to avoid accidental clicks.

evan: Great. If we implement this, teams will have a quick, auditable way to stop risky prewarms and satisfy compliance. Closing thread, RFC addendum incoming.
